## A GitHub repository card in the header

When the docs know their GitHub repository (from `source_url`), the header shows a card like the ones on well-known project sites: the GitHub logo, `owner/repo`, and below it the latest release, stars, and forks.

- The repository name is part of the page, so it shows without JavaScript.
- The release, stars, and forks load from GitHub in the reader's browser, once per session, so builds stay offline. Each appears only when there is something to show; forks stay hidden at 0. The release comes from the latest GitHub release, or the newest tag when there are none.
- On phones only the GitHub logo shows.

### Fixes

- The header no longer pushes the GitHub link and theme toggle off narrow screens, and the logo no longer shrinks.

### Upgrading

Nothing to change. A header part ejected from an earlier version keeps its star count; eject `header` again to get the card.
